item.dc:creator: Cariboo Signals Reviews
item.description:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 38703190050.

The run that didn't need to fall back, and the script that didn't hit its target

The primary run started at 1:05 AM Pacific, finished at 1:35 AM Pacific, and completed with a success conclusion, zero minutes late. Two fallbacks were scheduled behind it. Fallback 1 started and finished at 2:05 AM Pacific, also a success. Fallback 2, at 3:05 AM Pacific, is the run producing this review. The fallbacks were redundancy, not repair: nothing in the primary's record marks it as failed.

The more instructive mismatch is in the script. The first draft came in at 2,246 words against a target of 3,400. The pipeline sent it back for up to two expand passes, and the script that shipped ran 3,085 words. That is still 315 words short of target. The pipeline did not reach its own goal; it stopped at a figure it judged acceptable, and the facts do not record why that figure and not another.

Roundup coverage: 56 stories cut, and a count that doesn't match

The roundup pool held stories the airtime budget could not carry. 56 were dropped. This is by design: the pool is larger than one segment can air, and a cut story can return on a day when it fits the episode better. The 56 are deferred, not discarded.

Citation alignment on the roundup was 12 of 15 matched. Three roundup citations did not align with the script. The deep dives were worse on the same measure: 2 of 3 matched, so one deep-dive citation went unmatched. Those are the only places where the script and its sources diverge in the record, and the facts do not say which claims the unmatched citations supported.

Three deep dives, one debate, and a voice that leans one way

The three deep dives were a legal action by the FSIN against Ottawa over an audit clawback, a survivors' account from Eagle Feather News, and a return of an ancestral tipi cover reported by IndigiNews. The debate question put to the episode was who holds authority to judge Indigenous governments' financial records, cultural objects, and services, and whether sovereignty survives federal funding conditions and clawbacks.

On voice, the ratio of Casey to Riley lines was 0.9. The script contained zero AI-tell pattern hits. Neither figure is a failure, but the 0.9 ratio means the two hosts were close to balanced in line count, which is the number the pipeline is built to hold.

What shipped, and where it went

The audio runs 19.1 minutes and weighs 17.5 MB. The video runs 19.1 minutes at 66.7 MB, the same runtime as the audio. The RSS feed now carries 260 episodes. The generation step consumed 61,810 Anthropic input tokens across 18 Claude calls, alongside 19 brave-search calls and 4 brave-answers calls. Those are token and call counts, not spend, and the facts give no cost figure.

The slowest step was the script generation at 617 seconds, with checkout at 407 seconds and the GitHub Pages deploy at 350 seconds. Audio rendering took 206 seconds, publish 81 seconds, and the video upload 67 seconds. Every step concluded in success. The run had no warnings to report.

The show was short and the pipeline padded it

The first script draft came in at 2230 words against a target of 3400. The pipeline sent it back for up to two expand passes. What shipped was 3237 words, which is 163 words under target, not on it. The draft ran 1170 words short of target, so the expand passes recovered most of the gap but not all of it.

The expand passes did not add new reporting. The body backfill that would have filled thin articles ran out of budget: Brave body-backfill calls were spent at 12. The remaining thin articles kept their stub bodies, and the pipeline flagged them as possibly cut for sparseness. So the listener got a longer script built partly from articles that had little to say, and some of those may have been dropped anyway.

Fifty-three roundup stories were cut, and that was the design

The roundup pool was larger than one segment could air. The airtime budget (NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT) cut 53 stories. Those stories remain in the pool and can resurface on a day that matches them better. Nothing about the cut is a failure. It is the cost of a fixed airtime budget against a larger pool.

The count sits next to the sparse-body problem. The pipeline had room to air 53 fewer stories than it curated, yet it still had to expand a short draft and still kept thin articles it could not fill. The curated count and the aired count disagree in the direction of more material than airtime, while the script disagrees in the direction of less material than target. Both are true on the same run.

Citations held on the roundup and slipped on the deep dives

All 15 roundup citations matched their sources. On the deep dives, 1 of 3 citations matched. The three deep-dive stories were Hackster items on a package-measuring system, lakebed mapping, and protecting a Raspberry Pi 5 from sudden power loss. The two unmatched citations were the weakest link in an otherwise clean run, and the facts do not say why they failed to match.

The Casey-to-Riley voice ratio came in at 0.88, and the AI-tell pattern check recorded 0 hits. The check is clean, but a 0.88 ratio means the two hosts sat close to each other in how much they spoke, not that the dialogue was balanced in any stronger sense.

Audio held, short TTS takes were retried

The audio runs 18.8 minutes at 17.2 MB. The video runs 18.8 minutes at 65.2 MB. Two TTS takes came back shorter than their word count predicted. Each was retried once, and both retries were still short. The pipeline kept the longer take in each case, so no text was dropped from the episode. The short takes are a fact about the audio's pacing; the facts do not say whether they affected how the lines sounded.

Three runs, all green, one still running

The primary run started at 1:05 AM Pacific and finished at 1:32 AM Pacific, with no minutes late. Fallback 1 started and finished at 2:05 AM Pacific. Fallback 2, at 3:05 AM Pacific, is the run producing this review and has no finish time yet. Two of the three runs completed, and the first two both succeeded. The generate-script step took 610 seconds, the longest in the run, and the deploy step took 366 seconds. The episode count stands at 259.

Spend, by service

The run used 62,399 Anthropic input tokens. Brave search was called 28 times, Claude 17 times, and Brave answers 4 times. Those numbers measure calls and tokens, not cost, and the facts give no dollar figure. The 12 Brave body-backfill calls that exhausted their budget are part of the 28 search calls.

What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 38036684810.

Two of three TTS retries stayed short, and the pipeline kept the longer take

The audio render flagged three TTS takes that came back shorter than their word count predicts. Each was retried once. Two of the three retries were still short. The pipeline kept the longer of the two takes for each, so nothing was dropped from the episode. The recorded effect is that the retried takes were the longer of two imperfect results, not clean renders. The facts do not say how much of the episode each short take covered.

The territory check ran out of lookups and passed names it never verified

The territory check has a ceiling of 8 lookups per run. It hit that ceiling and left eight names unchecked: Lorne, Doerkson, Conservative, Elections, Denice, Bardua, Greens, Randy, and Transit. The count is nine because the ceiling warning repeats once per name after the eighth lookup; the unchecked names are the ones that matter. Several are proper names of people and parties, and the check that would confirm or reject a territorial attribution for them did not run.

The check did act on two cases. Sinixt and Nuxalk were both named in connection with the Tribune, which the territory map attributes to KâÃ³moks, Hulâqumiânum Treaty Group, É¬aÊamÉ©n gÉ©Ç°É (Tlaâamin), and Homalco. Two sentences kept an unsupported nation after the rewrite, and the rewrite was rejected. The pipeline did not fix those sentences. The facts record the rejection and do not record what the listener heard in their place.

The roundup pool dropped 59 stories, and only 10 of 15 roundup citations matched

The airtime budget (NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT) cut 59 stories from the roundup pool. That cut is by design: the pool is larger than one segment can air, and a cut story can return on a day when it fits better. The same day's citation check matched 10 of 15 roundup citations. The five unmatched citations are the discrepancy to watch. The deep dive matched all five of its citations.

The script's word count was 3681, and the audio ran 22.3 minutes at 20.4 MB. The video is 78.9 MB at the same 22.3 minutes. The episode was built from a larger pool than it aired, and it cited 15 roundup sources, 5 of which the citation check could not match to the script.

The debate question asks what the metrics measure

The episode's debate question was: what do local election and governance metrics (early votes, acclamations, candidate counts, forum attendance, budgets, ridership) actually measure, and do they still track the civic participation they claim to represent? The five deep dives were on Cariboo-region election coverage, a free-transit story, and a provincial income-tax proposal. The question asks the audience to test the numbers the coverage relies on. Those are the same numbers the pipeline's own roundup selected from. The facts do not show whether the episode answered the question.

Quality checks passed, and the run finished on time

The AI-tell pattern check returned 0 hits. The voice ratio, Casey over Riley, was 0.69. All three runs today (the primary at 1:05 AM Pacific and fallbacks at 2:05 AM and 3:05 AM Pacific) reported success, with zero minutes late for the primary and both fallbacks. The primary run was created at 1:05 AM Pacific and finished at 1:30 AM Pacific. The fallback at 3:05 AM Pacific is this review's own run and is still in progress. The API spend was 55,715 Anthropic input tokens, with 51 brave-search calls and 15 Claude calls. The slowest step was script generation at 594 seconds, followed by audio rendering at 317 seconds.
